assignedReviews.card_evidence: Motion is a change in position over a time interval
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: design and construct a simple electrical circuit to identify what materials will conduct electricity and use it to identify materials from the environment that will and will not conduct electricity
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines motion as a change in position over time. G5-F-9 is about designing and constructing a simple electrical circuit to identify conductors and insulators. There is no overlap in subject matter.

copy.en: Motion is a change in position over a time interval, like a tricycle moving from one corner to another.
copy.tl: Ang motion ay pagbabago ng posisyon sa loob ng isang time interval, tulad ng traysikel na umaandar mula sa isang kanto papunta sa kabila.
copy.bis: Ang motion mao ang pagbag-o sa posisyon sa usa ka time interval, sama sa traysikol nga molihok gikan sa usa ka eskina ngadto sa lain.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Radiation is the process of emitting energy through space, carried by particles or waves like sunlight.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to describe and illustrate the reflection of light using plane and curved mirrors and the refraction of light using transparent blocks, lenses, and prisms with examples from everyday applications
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is specifically about guided investigations into reflection of light using mirrors and refraction using lenses/prisms. The card defines radiation generally and does not address reflection or refraction at all.

copy.en: Radiation is the process of emitting energy through space, carried by particles or waves like sunlight.
copy.tl: Ang radiation ay ang proseso ng pagpapalabas ng enerhiya sa kalawakan, dala ng mga particle o waves tulad ng sikat ng araw.
copy.bis: Ang radiation mao ang proseso sa pagpagawas ug enerhiya pinaagi sa kawanangan, dala sa mga particle o waves sama sa kahayag sa adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Vibrations are quick back-and-forth movements, like a ruler twanging on the edge of a desk.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate through guided investigation the advantages and limitations of simple machines, such as inclined planes, wedges, levers, and pulleys
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines vibrations, which is a concept related to sound and waves. G6-F-2 is about simple machines (inclined planes, wedges, levers, pulleys) and their advantages/limitations. There is no mention of simple machines or any related content, so the card does not support this competency.

copy.en: Vibrations are quick back-and-forth movements, like a ruler twanging on the edge of a desk.
copy.tl: Ang vibrations ay mabilis na paggalaw pabalik-balik, tulad ng ruler na kumakalembang sa gilid ng mesa.
copy.bis: Ang vibrations kay paspas nga paglihok balik-balik, sama sa ruler nga nagtingog sa kilid sa lamesa.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Divide the wheel's radius by the axle's radius!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain in terms of the particle model the processes underlying convection and conduction of heat energy
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches how to calculate the mechanical advantage of a wheel and axle. G7-F-10 requires explaining convection and conduction of heat energy using the particle model. The card provides no information about heat transfer, particle motion, convection, or conduction, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en:
How do you calculate the mechanical advantage of a wheel and axle?

Divide the wheel's radius by the axle's radius! A wheel with a 100 cm radius and an axle with a 20 cm radius has an MA of 5.
copy.tl:
Paano mo kinakalkula ang mechanical advantage ng wheel and axle?

Hatiin ang radius ng wheel sa radius ng axle! Ang wheel na may 100 cm na radius at axle na may 20 cm na radius ay may MA na 5.
copy.bis:
Giunsa nimo pagkalkula ang mechanical advantage sa wheel and axle?

Bahina ang radius sa wheel sa radius sa axle! Ang wheel nga adunay 100 cm nga radius ug axle nga adunay 20 cm nga radius adunay MA nga 5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The point of application is the exact spot where a force is applied
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the physics concepts of point of application and line of action of a force. It has no relation to landforms, bodies of water, or their influence on living/non-living components.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The point of application is the exact spot where a force is applied
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about force application, not about locating or describing non-living things like rocks, soil, water, air, etc. It does not support the G3-E-1 competency.

copy.en: The point of application is the exact spot where a force is applied, and the line of action is the straight line it follows.
copy.tl: Ang point of application ay ang eksaktong lugar kung saan inilalapat ang force, at ang line of action ay ang tuwid na linyang sinusundan nito.
copy.bis: Ang point of application mao ang eksaktong lugar diin gipahamtang ang force, ug ang line of action mao ang tul-id nga linya nga ginasundan niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a bouncing ball loses momentum, that lost momentum is not destroyed; it is transferred to sound, heat, or the deformation of the surface it hit.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: construct and label simple graphs of different speeds including stationary and uniform speeds, both fast and slow
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses momentum transfer and energy conversion, not constructing or labeling graphs of speeds. It provides no support for the competency's graphing skill.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a bouncing ball loses momentum, that lost momentum is not destroyed; it is transferred to sound, heat, or the deformation of the surface it hit.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe uniform velocity and represent it using distance-time graphs
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about momentum loss and energy transfer, not about uniform velocity or distance-time graphs. It does not address the competency's content.

copy.en: When a bouncing ball loses momentum, that lost momentum is not destroyed; it is transferred to sound, heat, or the deformation of the surface it hit.
copy.tl: Kapag nawalan ng momentum ang tumatalbog na bola, hindi iyon nasisira; naililipat ito sa tunog, init, o pagka-deform ng surface na tinamaan nito.
copy.bis: Kung mawad-an og momentum ang nag-bounce nga bola, dili kana malaglag; mabalhin kini sa tingog, init, o pagkadeform sa surface nga naigo niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind direction is the direction from which the wind is blowing
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains wind direction, a weather concept. It provides no information about physical vs. chemical changes, reversibility, or any matter-related content required by G6-M-3.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wind direction is the direction from which the wind is blowing
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about wind direction and has no content on chemical bonds, bond formation/breaking, or chemical change, which are the focus of G9-M-2.

copy.en: Wind direction is the direction from which the wind is blowing, and it can be north, south, east, west, or in between.
copy.tl: Ang wind direction ay ang direksyon kung saan nanggagaling ang hangin, at maaari itong hilaga, timog, silangan, kanluran, o sa pagitan nito.
copy.bis: Ang wind direction mao ang direksyon diin naggikan ang hangin, ug kini mahimong norte, sur, silangan, kasadpan, o sa taliwala.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without homeostasis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses homeostasis and cell function, which is a biology topic. G4-M-3 concerns chemical properties of materials (burning, reactivity, degradability). No instructional support for that competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Without homeostasis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate proper handling and disposal of materials according to their properties, such as reusing objects, disposing of excess oil into garbage, and recycling paper, plastic or glass
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about homeostasis and survival, not about handling or disposal of materials. G3-M-7 is unrelated to the card's content.

copy.en:
What happens if your body cannot keep its balance?

Without homeostasis, your cells cannot work properly, so your health and even your survival are at risk!
copy.tl:
Ano ang mangyayari kung hindi mapanatili ng katawan mo ang balanse?

Kung walang homeostasis, hindi gagana nang maayos ang mga cells mo, kaya nanganganib ang kalusugan at maging ang buhay mo!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang mahitabo kung dili mapadayon sa imong lawas ang balanse?

Kung walay homeostasis, ang imong mga cells dili makalihok ug tarong, mao nga ang imong panglawas ug bisan ang imong kinabuhi nameligro!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At noon, the Sun is directly overhead, so its rays hit the ground at a 90-degree angle and concentrate the most energy on a small area.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe changes of state for solids, liquids, and gases as melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation using diagrams and flowcharts
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why noon is hottest due to the Sun's rays hitting at a 90-degree angle, concentrating energy. It does not address changes of state (melting, evaporation, freezing, condensation) or use diagrams/flowcharts, so it does not support G6-M-1.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: At noon, the Sun is directly overhead, so its rays hit the ground at a 90-degree angle and concentrate the most energy on a small area.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in temperature cause matter to change in state, such as solid to liquid to gas
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses solar angle and energy concentration, not how changes in temperature cause matter to change state (solid to liquid to gas). It is unrelated to G5-M-6.

copy.en:
Why is it hottest at noon?

At noon, the Sun is directly overhead, so its rays hit the ground at a 90-degree angle and concentrate the most energy on a small area.
copy.tl:
Bakit pinakamainit sa tanghali?

Sa tanghali, diretso sa itaas ang araw, kaya tumatama ang sinag nito sa lupa sa 90-degree angle at nakokonsentra ang pinakamaraming energy sa maliit na lugar.
copy.bis:
Ngano pinakainit sa udto?

Sa udto, ang adlaw naa diretso sa taas, busa ang iyang silaw moigo sa yuta sa 90-degree nga anggulo ug mag-concentrate sa pinakadaghang energy sa gamay nga lugar.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What made Fe del Mundo want to become a doctor?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the similarities and differences between electric motors and electric generators
assignedReviews.reason: The card is a biography of Fe del Mundo's motivation to study medicine. It contains no information about electric motors or electric generators, which is the subject of G10-F-11.

copy.en:
What made Fe del Mundo want to become a doctor?

When she was young, her older sister died, and that sad event pushed her to study medicine so she could help the poor and the sick.
copy.tl:
Ano ang nagtulak kay Fe del Mundo na maging isang doktor?

Noong bata pa siya, namatay ang kaniyang nakatatandang kapatid na babae, at ang malungkot na pangyayaring iyon ang nagtulak sa kaniya na mag-aral ng medisina upang makatulong sa mga mahihirap at may sakit.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang nagtulak kang Fe del Mundo nga mahimong usa ka doktor?

Sa bata pa siya, namatay ang iyang magulang nga babaye, ug kining masulub-on nga panghitabo maoy nagtulak kaniya sa pagtuon ug medisina aron makatabang sa mga pobre ug mga masakiton.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your two eyes each see a slightly different view
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains depth perception from having two eyes. It does not describe outer body parts of animals (head, legs, wings) or their role in movement and gathering food. The eye is not among the listed parts, and the function described is vision, not locomotion or feeding.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your two eyes each see a slightly different view
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses binocular vision and depth perception. G4-L-1 requires describing the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, or respiratory systems. The eyes and vision are not part of any of these systems, so the card does not support this competency.

copy.en:
Why do we have two eyes?

Your two eyes each see a slightly different view, letting your brain judge depth and distance — that's how you can catch a ball or tell how far something is!
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo may dalawang mata?

Bahagyang magkaiba ang nakikita ng bawat mata mo, kaya kaya ng utak mong husgahan ang lalim at distansya — kaya mo kayang saluhin ang bola o malaman kung gaano kalayo ang isang bagay!
copy.bis:
Nganong duha ang atong mata?

Gamayng lahi ang makita sa matag mata mo, mao nga mahukman sa utok ang giladmon ug gilay-on — mao nga masalo nimo ang bola o mahibaw-an kon unsa kalayo ang usa ka butang!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Water helps control body temperature, carries nutrients, removes wastes, and helps break down food for energy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a physical model or use drawings to demonstrate how the tilt of the Earth relative to its orbit around the Sun affects the intensity of sunlight absorbed by different areas of Earth over a year
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains the biological importance of water for living things (temperature control, nutrient transport, waste removal, digestion). The competency G7-E-10 requires demonstrating how Earth's axial tilt relative to its orbit affects sunlight intensity over a year. There is no connection to Earth's tilt, orbit, sunlight, or seasons.

copy.en:
Why do living things need water so much?

Water helps control body temperature, carries nutrients, removes wastes, and helps break down food for energy!
copy.tl:
Bakit kailangang-kailangan ng mga may buhay ang tubig?

Ang tubig ay tumutulong sa pagkontrol ng temperatura ng katawan, pagdadala ng nutrients, pagtatanggal ng dumi, at pagtunaw ng pagkain para sa energy!
copy.bis:
Nganong gikinahanglan kaayo sa mga buhing butang ang tubig?

Ang tubig makatabang sa pagkontrol sa temperatura sa lawas, pagdala sa nutrients, pagtangtang sa hugaw, ug pagtunaw sa pagkaon alang sa energy!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There's fluid in your inner ear that senses balance.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is specifically about the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. The card discusses the inner ear and balance, which is not one of these systems and does not support describing how any of them work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: There's fluid in your inner ear that senses balance.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The competency is about characteristics of living things: grow, respond, and reproduce. The card explains dizziness from spinning, which does not address growth, response, or reproduction as characteristics of living things.

copy.en:
Why do we get dizzy after spinning?

There's fluid in your inner ear that senses balance. When you stop spinning, the fluid keeps swirling, so your brain thinks you're still turning!
copy.tl:
Bakit tayo nahihilo pagkatapos umikot?

May likido sa loob ng tainga mo na nakakaramdam ng balanse. Kapag huminto ka, patuloy pa ring gumagalaw ang likido, kaya akala ng utak mo umiikot ka pa rin!
copy.bis:
Nganong maglipong ta human magtuyok?

Adunay likido sa sulod sa imong dalunggan nga makabati sa balanse. Kon mohunong ka, magpadayon og tuyok ang likido, mao nga maghunahuna ang imong utok nga nagtuyok pa gihapon ka!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because the wind blows stronger and steadier higher up in the sky!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe kinetic energy as the movement of objects or particles, and potential energy as energy stored due to the position of objects or particles
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains why wind turbine towers are tall due to stronger wind at height. It does not describe kinetic energy as movement of objects/particles or potential energy as stored due to position. The content is unrelated to the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Because the wind blows stronger and steadier higher up in the sky!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses wind strength at altitude, not sources or uses of light, sound, or heat energy. Wind energy is not covered by this competency, so the tag is incorrect.

copy.en:
Why are wind turbine towers so tall?

Because the wind blows stronger and steadier higher up in the sky!
copy.tl:
Bakit napakataas ng mga tore ng turbina?

Dahil mas malakas at mas matatag ang hangin sa mas mataas na lugar!
copy.bis:
Nganong taas kaayo ang mga tore sa turbine?

Tungod kay mas kusog ug mas lig-on ang hangin sa mas habog nga dapit!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Connecting wires are the paths that let charges travel from the voltage source to the load and back again.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that forces act between objects and can be measured
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the role of connecting wires in an electric circuit (charge flow between voltage source and load). G7-F-1 is about forces acting between objects and being measured; the card provides no information about forces or their measurement.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Connecting wires are the paths that let charges travel from the voltage source to the load and back again.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and demonstrate different ways to make objects move by natural causes, such as wind and water, or by people, such as pushing, pulling, rolling, and carrying
assignedReviews.reason: G3-F-1 concerns making objects move by natural causes or by people (pushing, pulling, rolling, carrying). The card is about electric charge flow in a circuit, not about moving objects by forces.

copy.en: Connecting wires are the paths that let charges travel from the voltage source to the load and back again.
copy.tl: Ang connecting wires ay ang mga daanan na nagpapahintulot sa charges na maglakbay mula sa voltage source papunta sa load at pabalik.
copy.bis: Ang connecting wires mao ang mga agianan nga nagtugot sa charges nga mobiyahe gikan sa voltage source ngadto sa load ug balik.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wood and rocks are insulators, meaning they do not allow heat and electricity to flow through them easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses thermal and electrical insulation properties of wood and rocks, which is unrelated to photosynthesis and respiration processes or their raw materials and products.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Wood and rocks are insulators, meaning they do not allow heat and electricity to flow through them easily
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using information from secondary sources identify the different parts of the cell where photosynthesis and respiration occur
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not mention cell parts, photosynthesis, or respiration; it is about material insulation properties, not cellular biology.

copy.en: Wood and rocks are insulators, meaning they do not allow heat and electricity to flow through them easily, so they stay cooler and safer to touch.
copy.tl: Ang kahoy at bato ay mga insulator, ibig sabihin hindi nila pinapadaan nang maayos ang init at kuryente, kaya nananatili silang mas malamig at ligtas hawakan.
copy.bis: Ang kahoy ug bato mga insulator, nagpasabot nga dili nila sayon nga ipaagi ang init ug kuryente, busa magpabilin silang mas bugnaw ug luwas hikapon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Work is the result of transmitting a force to an object, and machines transmit force to do desirable work.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify local examples of natural landforms and bodies of water such as mountains, valleys, rivers, and coastlines, and describe how they influence non-living and living components of the environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses work and force (physics concepts), while G5-E-1 requires identifying local landforms and bodies of water and describing their influence on the environment. There is no overlap in subject matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Work is done when a force moves an object over a distance
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe some effects of weather disturbances that occur in or near the Philippines
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches the physics concept of work (force × distance), which is unrelated to the competency about describing effects of weather disturbances in the Philippines. The topic is a physics/mechanics concept, not an Earth/space weather topic.

copy.en: Work is done when a force moves an object over a distance, like pushing a cart across the floor.
copy.tl: Nagkakaroon ng work kapag ang puwersa ay nagpapagalaw ng bagay sa isang distansya, tulad ng pagtulak ng cart sa sahig.
copy.bis: Adunay work kon ang puwersa makapalihok sa butang sa usa ka distansya, sama sa pagtulod sa cart sa salog.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The video phone was first shown at the New York World Fair
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: gather information from secondary sources to explain: a. how typhoons develop, and b. why the Philippines is prone to typhoons
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about the historical debut of the video phone at a world fair. It contains no information about typhoon development or why the Philippines is prone to typhoons, which is the subject of G8-E-7.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The video phone was first shown at the New York World Fair
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe typical weather conditions before, during, and after a tropical cyclone
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses a technology invention and its spread, not weather conditions before, during, or after a tropical cyclone. It provides no support for G5-E-10.

copy.en: The video phone was first shown at the New York World Fair, where it caused quite a stir, and later it was used all over the world.
copy.tl: Ang video phone ay unang ipinakita sa New York World Fair, kung saan ito ay pinag-usapan ng marami, at kalaunan ay ginamit na sa buong mundo.
copy.bis: Ang video phone unang gipakita sa New York World Fair, diin kini nakapahinam sa mga tawo, ug sa ulahi gigamit na sa tibuok kalibutan.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: covalent compound's formula
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card teaches writing chemical formulas for covalent compounds, a Grade 9 chemistry topic. It has no relation to observing natural objects in the sky, which is the subject of G3-E-6.

copy.en: You can write a covalent compound's formula from its name by using the prefixes to count the atoms of each element.
copy.tl: Maaari mong isulat ang formula ng isang covalent compound mula sa pangalan nito sa pamamagitan ng paggamit ng mga prefix para bilangin ang mga atom ng bawat element.
copy.bis: Mahimo nimong isulat ang formula sa usa ka covalent compound gikan sa iyang ngalan pinaagi sa paggamit sa mga prefix aron maihap ang mga atom sa matag element.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How much energy does an X-ray carry at a frequency of 5 x 10^17 Hz?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a Sun-Earth-Moon system model to demonstrate and explain the observable effects of predictable patterns and events including changes in seasons, changes observed in the patterns of visible star over a year, and solar and lunar eclipses
assignedReviews.reason: The card is a physics calculation of photon energy using E = hf, entirely unrelated to the Sun-Earth-Moon system model, seasons, star patterns, or eclipses described in G6-E-8.

copy.en:
How much energy does an X-ray carry at a frequency of 5 x 10^17 Hz?

Using E = hf, the energy is 3.315 x 10^-16 joules, a tiny but powerful amount!
copy.tl:
Gaano karaming energy ang dala ng X-ray sa frequency na 5 x 10^17 Hz?

Gamit ang E = hf, ang energy ay 3.315 x 10^-16 joules, isang napakaliit ngunit malakas na halaga!
copy.bis:
Pila ka energy ang dala sa X-ray sa frequency nga 5 x 10^17 Hz?

Gamit ang E = hf, ang energy kay 3.315 x 10^-16 joules, usa ka hilabihan ka gamay apan kusgan nga kantidad!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Gregorio Zara was such a good student that he was sent to study in the United States of America and then in France.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes Gregorio Zara's education abroad, which has no connection to magnets, their properties, or guided investigations about them. It does not support any part of the competency.

copy.en: Gregorio Zara was such a good student that he was sent to study in the United States of America and then in France.
copy.tl: Napakahusay na mag-aaral ni Gregorio Zara kaya ipinadala siya upang mag-aral sa United States of America at pagkatapos ay sa France.
copy.bis: Maayo kaayo nga estudyante si Gregorio Zara mao nga gipadala siya aron magtuon sa United States of America ug dayon sa France.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Abaca looks just like a banana plant and is actually its relative
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that abaca is a relative of the banana plant. It does not use a table, does not classify living things into the named groups (flowering/non-flowering plants, animal groups, microorganisms), and does not teach the skill of classification based on similar characteristics. The mention of being a relative is only loosely related to classification.

copy.en: Abaca looks just like a banana plant and is actually its relative — but don't try to eat its fruit, it's not good to eat!
copy.tl: Kamukha ng abaka ang puno ng saging at kamag-anak nga niya — pero huwag subukang kainin ang bunga nito, hindi ito makakain!
copy.bis: Susama sa saging ang abaka ug paryente gyud niya — apan ayaw pagsulay kaon sa bunga niini, dili gyud kini makaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Abaca is a Philippine plant known for its strong fiber called Manila hemp.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant but does not discuss outer parts (leaves, roots, stems) or their role in water/nutrient uptake. It only states that abaca produces a strong fiber, which is not the content of G3-L-5.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Abaca is a Philippine plant known for its strong fiber called Manila hemp.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the purpose of specialized structures in plants, such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, and aerial roots
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a plant fiber but does not describe the purpose of specialized structures such as rhizomes, tubers, thorns, bulbs, or aerial roots. Fiber is not one of the listed specialized structures, and no purpose is explained.

copy.en: Abaca is a Philippine plant known for its strong fiber called Manila hemp.
copy.tl: Ang abaka ay halamang Pilipino na kilala sa matibay na hibla nitong tinatawag na Manila hemp.
copy.bis: Ang abaka usa ka tanom sa Pilipinas nga bantogan sa lig-on nga lanot niini nga gitawag ug Manila hemp.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: strip or scrape the leaf stalks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions leaf stalks (a plant part) but does not address their role in getting water and nutrients from the soil; it describes fiber extraction instead.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: strip or scrape the leaf stalks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the root and shoot system in plants and describe why they are important
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to the shoot system (leaf stalks) but does not describe why the root and shoot system are important; it focuses on processing abaca fiber.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: strip or scrape the leaf stalks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes stripping/scraping as a process, but it is about removing pulp from plant stalks, not about changing solid materials (like shaping, pressing, hammering, joining, or cutting) to make them useful.

copy.en: To get clean abaca fiber, workers strip or scrape the leaf stalks to remove the soft pulp inside.
copy.tl: Para makuha ang malinis na hibla ng abaka, kinakayas o hinahagot ng mga manggagawa ang mga tangkay para matanggal ang malambot na laman.
copy.bis: Aron makuha ang limpyo nga lanot sa abaka, ginakayas o ginahagot sa mga mamumuo ang mga tangkay aron matangtang ang humok nga sulod.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its genus can be shortened to just the first letter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the importance of the six-kingdom system and the three-domain system of classification of living things
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains a binomial nomenclature abbreviation convention (shortening a genus to its initial after first use). It does not describe the six-kingdom or three-domain systems, nor their importance, so it provides no direct instructional support for G8-L-6.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: its genus can be shortened to just the first letter
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a table to show how living things can be classified into groups based on similar characteristics (plants including flowering and non-flowering; animals including mammals, reptiles, insects, birds, fish, amphibians; microorganisms including fungi and bacteria)
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about abbreviating a genus name, not about classifying living things into groups using a table. It does not support the table-based classification skill or the named groups in G5-L-4.

copy.en:
How do scientists shorten E. coli's name?

Once a scientific name has been written out in full, its genus can be shortened to just the first letter — like E. coli for Escherichia coli.
copy.tl:
Paano pinaikli ang pangalan ng E. coli?

Kapag nabanggit na nang buo ang isang pangalang siyentipiko, puwede na itong paikliin sa unang titik ng genus, gaya ng E. coli mula sa Escherichia coli.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagpamub-o ang ngalan sa E. coli?

Human masulat sa kumpleto kausa ang usa ka ngalang siyentipiko, mahimo na kining pamub-on sa unang letra sa genus, sama sa E. coli para sa Escherichia coli.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: yet animals still live there, adapted to survive it!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that animals are adapted to the abyssal zone but provides no specific example of an adaptation (e.g., mimicry, camouflage, or any concrete change). It does not teach the competency's skill of describing examples of how animals have changed to suit their environment.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ocean's abyssal zone (4,000–6,000 meters deep) is pitch dark, near-freezing (around 2–4°C), and under extreme pressure
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use a drawing or diagram to classify some Philippine animals and plants, based on their habitat: some live on land (terrestrial), live in water (aquatic) or fly in the air (aerial)
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a drawing or diagram, does not classify Philippine animals/plants, and does not address terrestrial, aquatic, or aerial habitats. The abyssal zone is not a Philippine habitat classification context for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The ocean's abyssal zone (4,000–6,000 meters deep) is pitch dark, near-freezing (around 2–4°C), and under extreme pressure
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe living things, such as animals and plants, as biotic factors and light, water, temperature, and soil type, as abiotic factors in an ecosystem
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions abiotic conditions (darkness, temperature, pressure) and that animals live there, but it does not explicitly describe living things as biotic factors or non-living things as abiotic factors in an ecosystem. It does not teach the biotic/abiotic factor distinction.

copy.en: The ocean's abyssal zone (4,000–6,000 meters deep) is pitch dark, near-freezing (around 2–4°C), and under extreme pressure — yet animals still live there, adapted to survive it!
copy.tl: Ang abyssal zone ng dagat (4,000–6,000 metro ang lalim) ay lubhang madilim, malamig (mga 2–4°C), at may sobrang presyon—pero may mga hayop pa ring nabubuhay doon, naka-angkop sa matinding kondisyong ito!
copy.bis: Ang abyssal zone sa dagat (4,000–6,000 metro ang giladmon) lubos ngitngit, bugnaw (mga 2–4°C), ug adunay grabeng presyon—apan adunay mga hayop nga nagpuyo gihapon didto, naka-angkop sa kining grabeng kondisyon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When a plate subducts, sediment on its surface is scraped off and piles up as an accretionary prism!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how the subduction of an oceanic plate impacts on the plate above it
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a feature of subduction (accretionary prism formation) but does not explain how subduction impacts the plate above it. No mention of the overriding plate or its effects.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's a chaotic, mixed pile of rocks found in front of subduction zones around the Philippines!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the structures, movements and events that occur at each type of plate boundary
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a structure at a convergent boundary (accretionary prism) but does not describe the structures, movements, or events of plate boundaries generally, nor does it cover the range of boundary types required by the competency.

copy.en:
What happens to the dirt and rocks when a tectonic plate dives underwater?

When a plate subducts, sediment on its surface is scraped off and piles up as an accretionary prism! It's a chaotic, mixed pile of rocks found in front of subduction zones around the Philippines!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa dumi at bato kapag sumisid ang tectonic plate?

Na-scrape ang sediment at nagtitipon bilang accretionary prism! Ito ay magulong, mixed na bato sa harapan ng subduction zone sa Pilipinas.
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa mga yuta ug bato kung mosalod ang usa ka tectonic plate?

Kon mosubduct ang plato, ang sediment sa ibabaw niini na-scrape ug nagtipon isip accretionary prism! Kini magulo, mixed nga pundok sa mga bato nga makita atubangan sa mga subduction zones sa palibot sa Pilipinas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When certain gases from factory and vehicle smoke mix with rain, it turns into "acid rain"
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the chemical properties of materials, such as they can be burnt, react with other materials, or are degradable or biodegradable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a chemical reaction (gases reacting with rain) and its effects, but it does not describe the chemical properties of materials such as being burnt, reacting with other materials, or being degradable/biodegradable in the sense of the competency. The reaction is presented as an environmental pollution phenomenon, not as a general property of materials. It shares vocabulary (react) but does not directly teach the competency.

copy.en: When certain gases from factory and vehicle smoke mix with rain, it turns into "acid rain" — a slightly sour rain that can hurt trees, lakes, and even stone statues!
copy.tl: Kapag humalo sa ulan ang ilang gas mula sa usok ng pabrika at sasakyan, nagiging "acid rain" ito — bahagyang maasim na ulan na makakasira ng mga puno, lawa, at maging mga bato at rebulto!
copy.bis: Kon ang pipila ka gas gikan sa aso sa pabrika ug sakyanan masagol sa ulan, mahimo kining "acid rain" — usa ka gamay nga aslom nga ulan nga makadaot sa mga kahoy, lanaw, ug bisan sa mga bato ug estatwa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: light movement like slow walking to help blood flow
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses active recovery and rest after exercise, mentioning blood flow, but does not describe how any human body system (muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, respiratory) works. It is only tangentially related to the circulatory system via blood flow.

copy.en: After heavy exercise, active recovery means light movement like slow walking to help blood flow, while complete rest means fully relaxing and doing nothing. Both matter.
copy.tl: Pagkatapos ng mabigat na ehersisyo, ang active recovery ay magaang galaw gaya ng dahan-dahang paglalakad para sa daloy ng dugo, habang ang complete rest ay talagang pagpapahinga nang husto. Pareho silang mahalaga.
copy.bis: Human sa bug-at nga ehersisyo, ang active recovery gaan nga lihok sama sa hinay nga paglakaw aron makatabang sa dagayday sa dugo, samtang ang complete rest mao ang hingpit nga pagpahulay. Parehong importante kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An adaptation is a feature that helps an animal or plant survive
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to describe examples of how some animals have changed to better suit their environment, such as mimicry or camouflage
assignedReviews.reason: The card defines adaptation generally and gives examples (thick fur, long beak) but does not describe how animals have changed over time to suit their environment, nor does it use secondary sources or mention mimicry/camouflage. It shares vocabulary but does not directly support the competency's skill of describing examples of evolutionary change.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: An adaptation is a feature that helps an animal or plant survive
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions plants and survival but gives no example of plants adapting to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods. It does not explain any specific plant adaptation, so it only relates to the topic of adaptation without teaching the competency.

copy.en:
What is an adaptation?

An adaptation is a feature that helps an animal or plant survive — like thick fur for the cold or a long beak to reach food!
copy.tl:
Ano ang adaptation?

Ang adaptation ay katangian na tumutulong sa hayop o halaman na mabuhay — tulad ng makapal na balahibo sa lamig o mahabang tuka para umabot sa pagkain!
copy.bis:
Unsa ang adaptation?

Ang adaptation usa ka kinaiya nga makatabang sa hayop o tanom nga mabuhi — sama sa baga nga balhibo para sa katugnaw o taas nga sungo aron makab-ot ang pagkaon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your adrenal glands are two small glands sitting on top of each kidney.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the location and function of adrenal glands (endocrine system), but the competency requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion. The card uses no such representation and does not address systems working together or the named examples.

copy.en:
Where are your adrenal glands?

Your adrenal glands are two small glands sitting on top of each kidney. They make hormones that help your body handle stress.
copy.tl:
Saan matatagpuan ang adrenal glands?

Ang adrenal glands ay dalawang maliit na glandula na nasa ibabaw ng bawat bato (kidney). Gumagawa ito ng mga hormone na tumutulong sa katawan na harapin ang stress.
copy.bis:
Asa nahimutang ang adrenal glands?

Ang adrenal glands maoy duha ka gamay nga glandula nga anaa sa ibabaw sa matag kidney. Naghimo kini og mga hormone nga motabang sa lawas nga atubangon ang stress.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it flows through the blood as a chemical messenger, reaching the heart, lungs, and muscles all at once.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how adrenaline travels via the blood, but it does not explain how the circulatory system works (heart, blood vessels, blood flow). It only mentions blood as a transport medium for a hormone, which is a specific example rather than instruction on the system's function.

copy.en: Adrenaline doesn't use nerves to send its orders — instead it flows through the blood as a chemical messenger, reaching the heart, lungs, and muscles all at once.
copy.tl: Hindi gumagamit ng nerve ang adrenaline para magpadala ng utos — sa halip, dumadaloy ito sa dugo bilang kemikal na mensahero, umaabot nang sabay-sabay sa puso, baga, at kalamnan.
copy.bis: Ang adrenaline dili mogamit og nerve aron magpadala og mando — hinuon, moagos kini sa dugo isip kemikal nga mensahero, moabot dungan sa kasingkasing, baga, ug kaunoran.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Adrenaline must attach to special cell parts called receptors, like a key fitting the right lock, before its message can work.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe homeostasis as a state of balance among all the body systems in humans that needs to be maintained for survival and proper functioning; its indicators include body temperature, glucose level, and blood pressure
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how adrenaline binds to receptors, but does not describe homeostasis as a state of balance among body systems or mention indicators such as body temperature, glucose level, or blood pressure. It is only tangentially related to body regulation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Adrenaline must attach to special cell parts called receptors, like a key fitting the right lock, before its message can work.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations, and it does not explain how body systems work together such as digestion and excretion. It only mentions a hormone-receptor interaction, which is not direct support for this competency.

copy.en:
How does adrenaline work in your body?

Adrenaline must attach to special cell parts called receptors, like a key fitting the right lock, before its message can work.
copy.tl:
Paano gumagana ang adrenaline sa katawan?

Kailangang dumikit ang adrenaline sa espesyal na bahagi ng selula na tinatawag na receptor, parang susing bumabagay sa tamang kandado, bago gumana ang mensahe nito.
copy.bis:
Unsaon paglihok sa adrenaline sa lawas?

Kinahanglan motapot ang adrenaline sa espesyal nga bahin sa selula nga gitawag og receptor, sama sa yawi nga mohaom sa husto nga kandado, aron molihok ang mensahe niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Once your milk teeth fall out, permanent teeth grow in
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use flow charts to compare the different stages in the life cycle of animals, such as a butterfly, frog, chicken, and human
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a single human developmental change (milk teeth replaced by permanent teeth). It does not use a flow chart, does not compare life-cycle stages, and does not address the life cycle of animals (butterfly, frog, chicken, human) as required by the competency. The content is only tangentially related to human growth.

copy.en: Once your milk teeth fall out, permanent teeth grow in — and those are meant to last you the rest of your life.
copy.tl: Kapag nalaglag na ang gatas na ngipin, tutubo ang permanenteng ngipin na para sa habambuhay na paggamit.
copy.bis: Kon matangtang na ang gatas nga ngipon, motubo ang permanente nga ngipon nga alang sa tibuok kinabuhi nga gamit.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Swallows and swifts are often busiest catching insects at dawn and dusk
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use information from secondary sources to group animals according to the food they eat: plant eaters (herbivores), meat eaters (carnivores), and plant and meat-eaters (omnivores)
assignedReviews.reason: Catching insects is not grouping animals as herbivores, carnivores, or omnivores.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Swallows and swifts are often busiest catching insects at dawn and dusk, when many insects fill the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web
assignedReviews.reason: Catching insects at dusk is not the roles of producers, consumers, scavengers, and decomposers in a food web.

copy.en: Swallows and swifts are often busiest catching insects at dawn and dusk, when many insects fill the air.
copy.tl: Madalas na masipag lumipad at kumain ng insekto ang mga layang-layang at swift tuwing madaling-araw at takipsilim kapag marami ang lumilipad na insekto.
copy.bis: Ang mga sayaw ug balinsasayaw kasagaran kugihan mudakop og insekto sa kaadlawon ug kilumkilom, kon daghan ang naglupad nga insekto.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: What happens after a big earthquake?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models or illustrations to explain how movements along faults generate earthquakes and identify and explain which types of faults are most likely to occur in the Philippines and explain why
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions aftershocks after a big earthquake. It does not use models or illustrations, explain fault movements, or identify Philippine fault types, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: You might feel smaller, follow-up tremors called aftershocks
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how the effects of earthquakes on communities depend on their magnitude
assignedReviews.reason: The card refers to a big earthquake and smaller aftershocks, but does not describe how earthquake effects on communities depend on magnitude. It is only tangentially related to earthquake magnitude.

copy.en:
What happens after a big earthquake?

You might feel smaller, follow-up tremors called aftershocks as the ground settles down!
copy.tl:
Anong nangyayari pagkatapos ng malakas na lindol?

Makakaramdam ka ng mas mahihinang pagyanig na tinatawag na aftershocks habang kumakalma ang lupa!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo human sa kusog nga linog?

Makabati ka og mas huyang nga mga pag-uyog nga gitawag og aftershocks samtang nagkalma ang yuta!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It's argon! This invisible gas makes up about 0.93% of the air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The competency requires describing air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor. The card only states that argon is the third most common gas at 0.93%, without mentioning any of the four required gases or describing air as a mixture of them. This is related to air composition but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
What's the third most common gas floating in the air around us?

It's argon! This invisible gas makes up about 0.93% of the air we breathe every single day.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ikatlong pinakamaraming gas na lumulutang sa hangin sa paligid natin?

Ito ang argon! Ang hindi nakikitang gas na ito ay bumubuo ng halos 0.93% ng hangin na hinihinga natin araw-araw.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang ikatulong labing daghang gas nga naglutaw sa hangin sa palibot nato?

Kini ang argon! Ang dili makita nga gas nga naghimo og mga 0.93% sa hangin nga among ginhangin matag adlaw.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Every time you breathe in, your body takes in wonderful oxygen straight from the air!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that we breathe in oxygen. It does not identify any parts of the respiratory system (nose, windpipe, lungs) or describe how they work, nor does it use pictures or diagrams as required by the competency.

copy.en: Every time you breathe in, your body takes in wonderful oxygen straight from the air!
copy.tl: Kapag huminga ka papasok, kumukuha ang katawan mo ng oxygen mula sa hangin!
copy.bis: Kon moginhawa ka pasulod, ang imong lawas magkuha og oxygen gikan sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: When air is heated, its particles gain energy, move faster, and spread farther apart, so the air expands and takes up more space.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: plan simple scientific investigations in answering questions, such as 'Do gases (like air) or liquids (like water) have mass?', using appropriate simple science equipment, such as a balance, and a thermometer, with appropriate units
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes particle behavior and expansion of heated air, but the competency requires planning a scientific investigation to answer whether gases or liquids have mass using equipment such as a balance and thermometer. The card does not address mass, measurement, or investigation planning.

copy.en: When air is heated, its particles gain energy, move faster, and spread farther apart, so the air expands and takes up more space.
copy.tl: Kapag nainitan ang hangin, nagkakaroon ng enerhiya ang mga particle nito, mas mabilis gumalaw, at nagkakalayo, kaya lumalawak ang hangin at sumasakop ng mas malaking espasyo.
copy.bis: Kung mainitan ang hangin, ang mga particle niini makakuha ug enerhiya, mas paspas nga molihok, ug magkabulag, mao nga molapad ang hangin ug mokuha ug mas dako nga espasyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Air isn't just one thing! It is actually a mixture of many different gases mixed together, not just a single substance.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe air as a mixture of oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, and water vapor
assignedReviews.reason: The card states that air is a mixture of many gases but does not name oxygen, carbon dioxide, nitrogen, or water vapor, so it does not directly support describing air as a mixture of those specific gases.

copy.en: Air isn't just one thing! It is actually a mixture of many different gases mixed together, not just a single substance.
copy.tl: Ang hangin ay hindi lang iisang bagay! Ito ay isang halo o mixture ng maraming iba't ibang gas, hindi lang iisang sangkap.
copy.bis: Ang hangin dili lang usa ka butang! Kini usa ka sagol o mixture sa daghang lain-laing gas, dili lang usa ka substansya.
